title: SBI aiming to up lending under 'MSME Dream' process to ₹50 crore
description:
The State Bank of India (SBI) aims to increase lending under its 'MSME Dream' product, which gives small businesses collateral-free digital loans, to Rs 50 crore by March 2027, a senior official said on Friday.
At present, the bank offers loans of up to Rs 5 crore under the product launched in December 2023 and there has been some Closed User Group (CUG) selling of loans up to Rs 10 crore at select branches, the official said.
"By November 30, we will increase the lending to Rs 10 crore across all branches and will launch a pilot project to do loans of Rs 50 crore each under the product on the same day," the official said.
The bank will increase the per loan borrowing under the product to Rs 50 crore across all branches by March next year, the official said.
The country's largest lender has sanctioned Rs 2.25 lakh crore under the 'Dream' product till now, the official said, stressing that the asset quality is also much better on such loans.
